correctness.rationale: For each oriented arrow, the commutator coefficient is a vertex-difference pivot plus a signed vertex-incidence row. Eliminating pivots gives the incidence rank of monochromatic nonzero-weight edges. In a simple connected unicyclic graph, the only possible incidence dependency is the full cycle, producing exactly one rank correction. Vertex differences on bridges are independent; those around the cycle satisfy one linear relation and have q lifts. Additive-character orthogonality gives \( ((q^2-1)^r+(q-1)(-1)^r)/q \) constrained nonzero-pair counts. The resulting polynomial has constant \(q\), positive top-degree coefficient and first-degree coefficient \(q(q-1)((q+1)n-qc)\). Every possible rank is constructible. The standalone direct-products verifier returned VERIFY_OK_UNICYCLIC 13 after enumerating every element of 13 small algebras, including F4.

value.rationale: Centralizer-dimension distributions and rank-one inner derivations are natural invariants of finite associative algebras. The closed formula treats all unicyclic shapes, orientations, sizes, and finite fields, and establishes a reconstruction classification: the polynomial determines q, n, and unique cycle length c, yet ignores tree-attachment locations. This is a structural invariant result beyond a first-moment commuting count, with a precise graph-theoretic boundary.
